svg.title: Verify the CSR before submission — instructional mockup
svg.desc: Step-specific guided recreation. Not a genuine screenshot or live result.
svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Verify the CSR before submission
Application server (TLS-APP01) · RHEL 9 Bash terminal · learner@10.90.0.10
RHEL 9 — learner@tls-app01
COMMAND / FILE CONTENT TO ENTER — PRESERVE CASE
openssl req -in ~/tls-work/app-v1.csr -noout -verify -subject -text
set -o pipefail
openssl req -in ~/tls-work/app-v1.csr -pubkey -noout | openssl pkey -pubin -outform DER | openssl
dgst -sha256
sudo openssl pkey -in /etc/pki/tls/private/app-v1.key -pubout -outform DER | openssl dgst -sha256
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
The signature verifies and the request contains DNS:app.example.mil. Wording can differ slightly
between OpenSSL versions. The two complete public-key digests must also be identical.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. Paste the block below. Read Certificate request self-signature verify OK, the subject, and Requested
Extensions.
2. Find X509v3 Subject Alternative Name and DNS:app.example.mil.
3. Only prepare this CSR for transfer if the signature and intended name both check out. The CA will
still need to approve the request.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
